div.head: V Atr 12.1
div.ab: ⁊ gyf man ænig lic of rihtscriftscire elles hwar lecge, gelæste man saulsceat swa þeh into þam mynstre, þe hit to hyrde.
⁊ gif man ænig lic of rihtscriftscire elles hwær lecge, gelæste man saulsceat swa þeh into þam mynstre, þe hit to hyrde.
⁊ gif man ænig lic of rihtscriftscire elles hwar lecge, gelæste man sawlsceat swa ðeah into ðam mynstre, þe hit to hirde.
⁊ gif man ænig lic of rihtscriftscire elles hwar lecge, gelæste man sawlsceat swa ðeah into ðam mynstre þe hit to hirde.
And gyf man ænig lic of rihtscriftscire elles hwar lecge, gelæste man saulsceat swa þeh into þam mynstre þe hit to hyrde.
Und wenn man eine Leiche ausserhalb ihres gesetzlichen Beichtsprengels anderswo bestattet, zahle man Seelengeld [für sie] dennoch in die Kirche, zu der sie gehört hat.
And if any body is buried elsewhere, outside its proper parish, let soul-scot [for it] nevertheless be paid to the minster to which it belonged.
And if any body is buried elsewhere than in the parish to which it properly belongs, the payment shall nevertheless be made to the church to which the deceased belonged.
And if any body is buried elsewhere, outside the proper parish, the payment for the soul is nevertheless to be paid to the minster to which it belonged.
And if any person’s body is buried other than in its proper parish, the dues should still be paid to the church to which he belonged.

note.label: retrospectively inserted from
note.quote: it may be little if at all older than Cnut's code of 1018 (5.), and that it was then retrospectively inserted into extant versions of 'V Æthelred' (1.)

note.seg: Nicht ‘er [der Seelschatz] zukommt’; hit bezieht sich auf lic, und hyrde ist Vergangenheit
Not ‘to which it [the soul-scot] is due’; hit refers to lic, and hyrde is past tense
Cf. II Edg. 5, 2; VI Atr. 21; I Cn. 13, 1; Anselm (1102): ne corpora defunctorum extra parochiam suam sepelienda portentur ut presbyter parochiae perdat quod inde illi juste debetur.
